result.note: Weekly roundup; tested the parliamentary handling of three Union bills and the US Senate tariff bill on Russian-oil buyers.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about legislation in Parliament in August 2026:
items: The Tribunals Reforms Bill was passed without debate.
The FCRA bill was referred to a joint parliamentary committee rather than being debated on the floor.
A bill on mineral rights sought to expand the powers of states to tax mineral rights.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the mineral-rights bill sought to strip states of the power to tax mineral rights, not expand it. TBB read the week's bills as the Centre moving power towards itself.
questions.source: A Tribunals Reforms Bill passed without debate on Monday, a bill to strip states of mineral-rights taxation followed on Thursday, and the FCRA bill went to a joint parliamentary committee the same day rather than being debated on the floor.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the US Senate passed a bill authorising tariffs of up to what level on buyers of Russian oil?
questions.explain: The Senate bill authorised tariffs of up to 100% on Russian-oil buyers. Within days, Nayara Energy shipped fuel refined from Russian oil back to Russia, giving Washington's critics the headline the bill was written to punish.
questions.source: The US Senate passed a bill authorising tariffs up to 100% on Russian-oil buyers on Saturday
